STEMforALL

Hands-on STEM for every kid.

STEMforALL is a student-led initiative that promotes equality in STEM. We run structured, sensory-friendly enrichment sessions that bring hands-on science and engineering to elementary students with cognitive disabilities.

Explore our kits Learn about us Get involved
About us

Everyone belongs in STEM.

STEMforALL is a student-led initiative that creates structured, sensory-friendly STEM workshops for elementary students with cognitive disabilities and any curious young learner. With our own hands-on kits, we build confidence and curiosity while introducing kids to the STEM careers they can pursue.

Interested in Engineering, Medicine, Business, Creative Arts, or more? Everyone is welcome!

  • Engineering
  • Medicine
  • Business
  • Creative Arts
  • And so much more

Our goals

Make STEM more accessible, build confidence, and open the door to future STEM careers.

What we do

We create our own STEM kits and lead workshops in elementary schools.

How we run

Structured, predictable, sensory-friendly sessions guided by student leaders.

STEMforALL: Motion & Statics Line

Four kits.
Four careers.

Each hands-on kit is tied to a real career. Together they explore how things move and how things stand.

Fling Jet

Career: Aerospace Engineering

This hands-on engineering activity introduces students to the science of flight, including aerodynamics, lift, and air resistance. As well as physics such as speed = distance/time.

Car

Career: Mechanical Engineering

This hands-on engineering activity introduces students to the science of motion. Students discover how forces influence a car’s movement and how different components work together to create motion.

Building

Career: Architecture

This hands-on structural engineering activity introduces students to stability, balance, and the forces acting on structures.

Bridge

Career: Civil Engineering

This hands-on engineering activity introduces students to structural design, stability, and load distribution. As well as understanding how adding more weight to the bridge causes the overall force the bridge must withstand to increase.
